She is the most passionate professor I've ever seen. Thanks to her, I became interested in the course content and learned a lot. When she does not know the answer to a question, she *actually* searches for the answer or at least directs us to where we can find it, which is really important I believe. By doing this, she teaches more than just the content of the course, you'll learn how to do research independently, where to find the sources, etc. She's very respectful, she never shames anyone for giving the wrong or partial answer, which also enhances language learning, I think. She is also very helpful, almost always creates time for your questions both in class and through her office hours. I have nothing bad to say about her, she is one of the best professors in Bilkent. I think among the archeology students, it is a known fact. I did not know her before taking the course, and even though the Hittite language was difficult at times, I am glad I was one of her students.

course:
Besides having an amazing teacher, the course is very well structured. All instructions were clear, and since the assignments were regular, preparing for quizzes and exams was much easier, which played an important role in improving overall language skills. A very positive aspect of the course is working with real documentation, which gives valuable insight into the philological side of studying a language.
Studying ancient languages, especially Anatolian ones like Hittite, at the university is a very rare and special opportunity, and I hope the course will continue/expand in the coming years.

Learning cuneiform was hard and took effort. For this class, I had to study every week. Eventually it will be easier and easier, but it is better to be ready to study consistently.

As the course goes on, the grammar requires a greater amount of your attention because there are an abundance of affixes (especially suffixes) that are akin to each other, and at some point in the course, if you do not pay much attention, it may become confusing. Latin I is a course that requires a lot of effort, but I think İlgi Hoca elucidated even the most difficult chapters and grammar rules for us, both through the assignments she gave and the intriguing materials she used in class.
